name: HAL HTT-40

what_it_is.prose: The HAL HTT-40 (Hindustan Turbo Trainer-40) is an indigenously designed single-engine turboprop basic trainer developed by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's Aircraft Research & Design Centre in Bengaluru to meet the Indian Air Force's Stage-I (basic) flying-training requirement. It was conceived to replace the HPT-32 Deepak piston trainer, which was grounded in 2009 after a fatal accident, and the prototype made its maiden flight in May 2016. On 1 March 2023 the Union Cabinet approved procurement of 70 HTT-40 aircraft from HAL for the IAF at a cost of Rs 6,828.36 crore, with the aircraft to be delivered over six years; trade reporting notes an option for a further 36 aircraft. The Cabinet release states the aircraft has approximately 56% indigenous content, to be raised above 60% through indigenisation of major components and subsystems, and projects roughly 1,500 direct jobs across more than 100 MSMEs. The principal import dependency is propulsion: the aircraft is powered by the Honeywell TPE331-12B turboprop, and under a $100 million contract signed in July 2022 Honeywell agreed to supply the first 16 engines from the USA before production of the remaining units transitions to HAL in India. Honeywell delivered the first three TPE331-12B engines to HAL on 11 June 2026 after supply-chain delays, keeping HAL on course to hand the first HTT-40s to the IAF. The HTT-40 will operate alongside the IAF's 75 Pilatus PC-7 Mk II in the basic-training role.

deployments_procurement.summary: The HTT-40's flagship order is the 70-aircraft, Rs 6,828.36 crore procurement from HAL approved by the Union Cabinet on 1 March 2023, for delivery over six years, with a reported option for 36 more. HAL earlier received the RFP for 70 aircraft at Aero India 2021. Deliveries hinge on the Honeywell TPE331-12B engine supply, the first three of which reached HAL on 11 June 2026.

faq.question: How many HTT-40 has the IAF ordered and at what cost?
faq.answer: The Union Cabinet approved procurement of 70 HTT-40 basic trainers from HAL on 1 March 2023 at a cost of Rs 6,828.36 crore, to be delivered over six years. Trade reporting notes an additional option for 36 aircraft.

faq.question: Is the HTT-40 indigenous, and what is its engine?
faq.answer: The HTT-40 is an indigenous HAL design with approximately 56% indigenous content, planned to rise above 60%. Its main import dependency is the engine: the Honeywell TPE331-12B turboprop, with the first 16 engines supplied from the USA before HAL takes up production of the remainder. Honeywell delivered the first three engines to HAL on 11 June 2026.

faq.question: What does the HTT-40 replace and what is its role?
faq.answer: The HTT-40 is a Stage-I (basic) flying trainer designed to replace the HPT-32 Deepak piston trainer, which was grounded in 2009. It made its maiden flight in May 2016 and will operate alongside the IAF's fleet of 75 Pilatus PC-7 Mk II basic trainers.
